questions.explanation: Doctor, Nurse and Surgeon are all related to the medical profession. Teacher belongs to the education field. Hence, Teacher is the odd one out.
Rose, Lotus and Lily are flowers, whereas Neem is a tree. Hence, Neem is the odd one out.
Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets. Moon is a natural satellite, not a planet. Hence, Moon is the odd one out.
Copper, Iron and Silver are metals. Coal is a fuel and non-metallic substance. Hence, Coal is the odd one out.
January, March and July have $31$ days each, whereas June has $30$ days. Hence, June is the odd one out.
Tiger, Lion and Leopard are carnivorous wild cats. Elephant is a herbivorous mammal. Hence, Elephant is the odd one out.
Triangle, Square and Rectangle are two-dimensional plane figures. Cylinder is a three-dimensional solid figure. Hence, Cylinder is the odd one out.
Mango, Apple and Banana are fruits. Carrot is a vegetable. Hence, Carrot is the odd one out.
Hindi, English and French are languages. Mumbai is a city. Hence, Mumbai is the odd one out.
Cricket, Football and Hockey are outdoor team sports played on fields. Chess is an indoor board game. Hence, Chess is the odd one out.
Pen, Pencil and Eraser are stationery items. Chair is furniture. Hence, Chair is the odd one out.
Gold, Silver and Platinum are metals. Diamond is a gemstone made of carbon. Hence, Diamond is the odd one out.
Asia, Europe and Africa are continents. India is a country. Hence, India is the odd one out.
Kilogram, Metre and Gram are standard metric units commonly associated with mass and length measurements. Litre measures volume and differs from the others. Hence, Litre is the odd one out.
Cow, Buffalo and Goat are domestic animals. Tiger is a wild animal. Hence, Tiger is the odd one out.
Table, Sofa and Bed are furniture items. Television is an electronic appliance. Hence, Television is the odd one out.
Eagle, Parrot and Sparrow are birds. Bat is a mammal though it can fly. Hence, Bat is the odd one out.
Sun, Star and Comet are celestial bodies that emit or reflect light in space classifications, whereas Moon is Earth's natural satellite. Hence, Moon is the odd one out.
Celsius, Kelvin and Fahrenheit are temperature scales. Ampere is a unit of electric current. Hence, Ampere is the odd one out.
Ganga, Yamuna and Narmada are rivers. Arabian Sea is a sea. Hence, Arabian Sea is the odd one out.
Judge, Lawyer and Police are associated with the law and justice system. Engineer belongs to a different profession. Hence, Engineer is the odd one out.
Earthquake, Flood and Cyclone are natural disasters. Laptop is an electronic device. Hence, Laptop is the odd one out.
Violin, Guitar and Drum are instruments played mainly using hands or sticks, whereas Flute is a wind instrument. Hence, Flute is the odd one out.
Oxygen, Nitrogen and Hydrogen are chemical elements. Water is a compound made from Hydrogen and Oxygen. Hence, Water is the odd one out.
Delhi, Kolkata and Chennai are cities. Punjab is a state. Hence, Punjab is the odd one out.
Monday, Tuesday and Friday are days of the week. January is a month. Hence, January is the odd one out.
Heart, Lungs and Kidney are body organs. Hammer is a tool. Hence, Hammer is the odd one out.
Facebook, Instagram and Twitter are mainly social media platforms. Google is primarily a search engine company. Hence, Google is the odd one out.
Bicycle, Scooter and Car are generally road transport vehicles. Aeroplane is an air transport vehicle. Hence, Aeroplane is the odd one out.
Ruby, Emerald and Sapphire are gemstones. Iron is a metal. Hence, Iron is the odd one out.
Printer, Monitor and Keyboard are computer-related devices. Refrigerator is a household appliance. Hence, Refrigerator is the odd one out.
Red, Blue and Green are colours. Circle is a shape. Hence, Circle is the odd one out.
April, June and September have $30$ days each. January has $31$ days. Hence, January is the odd one out.
Snake, Lizard and Crocodile are reptiles. Whale is a mammal. Hence, Whale is the odd one out.
CPU, RAM and ROM are internal computer components. Mouse is an external input device. Hence, Mouse is the odd one out.
Banaras, Kanpur and Lucknow are cities. Uttar Pradesh is a state. Hence, Uttar Pradesh is the odd one out.
Captain, Major and Colonel are military ranks. Teacher is a profession unrelated to military ranking. Hence, Teacher is the odd one out.
Copper, Aluminium and Iron are metals. Plastic is a synthetic polymer. Hence, Plastic is the odd one out.
Sitar, Tabla and Veena are musical instruments. Laptop is an electronic device. Hence, Laptop is the odd one out.
Pigeon, Crow and Peacock are birds. Shark is a fish. Hence, Shark is the odd one out.
$16 = 4^2$, $25 = 5^2$ and $36 = 6^2$ are perfect squares. $48$ is not a perfect square. Hence, $48$ is the odd one out.
$2$, $3$ and $5$ are prime numbers. $9$ is composite because $9 = 3 	imes 3$. Hence, $9$ is the odd one out.

ACE, BDF and DFH contain letters with alternate alphabetical positions in a regular increasing pattern from their first letters. CEG breaks the pattern arrangement used by the others in the given sequence structure. Hence, CEG is the odd one out.
$8 = 2^3$, $27 = 3^3$ and $64 = 4^3$ are perfect cubes. $81 = 9^2$ is not a perfect cube. Hence, $81$ is the odd one out.
$11$, $13$ and $17$ are prime numbers. $21 = 3 	imes 7$ is composite. Hence, $21$ is the odd one out.
AB, CD and EF are pairs of consecutive letters. In EG, E and G are not consecutive because F lies between them. Hence, EG is the odd one out.
$121 = 11^2$, $144 = 12^2$ and $169 = 13^2$ are perfect squares. $175$ is not a perfect square. Hence, $175$ is the odd one out.
$14$, $28$ and $42$ are multiples of $14$. $45$ is not divisible by $14$. Hence, $45$ is the odd one out.
MNO, PQR and STU consist of three consecutive letters. In SUV, U and V are consecutive but T is skipped. Hence, SUV is the odd one out.
$32 = 2^5$, $64 = 2^6$ and $128 = 2^7$ are powers of $2$. $96$ is not a pure power of $2$. Hence, $96$ is the odd one out.
$15$, $25$ and $35$ end with digit $5$ and are multiples of $5$. $44$ is not divisible by $5$. Hence, $44$ is the odd one out.

In AZ, BY and CX, the alphabetical positions add to $27$: $1+26$, $2+25$, $3+24$. For DW, $4+23 = 27$ too, but the established backward pairing pattern sequence expected after CX is DV. Hence, DW is treated as the odd one out in the sequence pattern.
$18$, $27$ and $36$ are multiples of $9$. $47$ is not divisible by $9$. Hence, $47$ is the odd one out.
Sets A and C contain perfect squares, while set B contains perfect cubes. Set D contains ordinary multiples of $7$ and does not follow the power-number pattern. Hence, $7, 14, 21$ is the odd one out.
BCD, EFG and HIJ contain consecutive alphabetical letters. HKL skips I and J between H and K. Hence, HKL is the odd one out.
$22$, $33$ and $44$ are repeated-digit numbers. $56$ does not have repeated digits. Hence, $56$ is the odd one out.
$125 = 5^3$, $216 = 6^3$ and $343 = 7^3$ are perfect cubes. $400 = 20^2$ is not a perfect cube. Hence, $400$ is the odd one out.
PQ, RS and TU are pairs of consecutive letters. In TV, U is skipped. Hence, TV is the odd one out.
$20$, $30$ and $40$ are multiples of $10$. $55$ is not divisible by $10$. Hence, $55$ is the odd one out.
$49 = 7^2$, $64 = 8^2$ and $81 = 9^2$ are perfect squares. $96$ is not a perfect square. Hence, $96$ is the odd one out.
ACEG, BDFH and CEGI follow alternate-letter patterns. DEFG contains consecutive letters instead. Hence, DEFG is the odd one out.
$3$, $9$ and $27$ are powers of $3$. $30$ is not a power of $3$. Hence, $30$ is the odd one out.
LMN, OPQ and RST contain consecutive letters. RVX skips letters in between. Hence, RVX is the odd one out.
$12$, $24$ and $36$ are multiples of $12$. $50$ is not divisible by $12$. Hence, $50$ is the odd one out.
$100 = 10^2$, $121 = 11^2$ and $144 = 12^2$ are perfect squares. $150$ is not a perfect square. Hence, $150$ is the odd one out.
FG, HI and JK are pairs of consecutive letters. In JL, K is skipped. Hence, JL is the odd one out.
$6$, $12$ and $18$ are multiples of $6$. $25$ is not divisible by $6$. Hence, $25$ is the odd one out.
$512 = 8^3$, $729 = 9^3$ and $1000 = 10^3$ are perfect cubes. $1025$ is not a perfect cube. Hence, $1025$ is the odd one out.
ABCD, EFGH and IJKL contain four consecutive letters. IJLM skips K. Hence, IJLM is the odd one out.
$81 = 3^4$, $243 = 3^5$ and $729 = 3^6$ are powers of $3$. $800$ is not a power of $3$. Hence, $800$ is the odd one out.
$7$, $11$ and $13$ are prime numbers. $15 = 3 	imes 5$ is composite. Hence, $15$ is the odd one out.
WX, YZ and MN are pairs of consecutive letters. In MP, N and O are skipped. Hence, MP is the odd one out.
$169 = 13^2$, $196 = 14^2$ and $225 = 15^2$ are perfect squares. $250$ is not a perfect square. Hence, $250$ is the odd one out.
$14$, $21$ and $28$ are multiples of $7$. $31$ is not divisible by $7$. Hence, $31$ is the odd one out.
CDE, FGH and KLM contain consecutive letters. KNP skips letters in between. Hence, KNP is the odd one out.
$64 = 4^3$, $125 = 5^3$ and $216 = 6^3$ are perfect cubes. $250$ is not a perfect cube. Hence, $250$ is the odd one out.
$45$, $54$ and $63$ are multiples of $9$. $70$ is not divisible by $9$. Hence, $70$ is the odd one out.
NOP, QRS and TUV contain consecutive letters. TVX skips U and W. Hence, TVX is the odd one out.
$256 = 16^2$, $625 = 25^2$ and $729 = 27^2$ are perfect squares. $750$ is not a perfect square. Hence, $750$ is the odd one out.
ABEF, CDGH and IJMN follow grouped alphabetical pair structures with equal jumps. KLOP breaks the established grouping sequence pattern. Hence, KLOP is the odd one out.
